name.text: Description 1 on Rules and properties of integration

questiontext.text:
Rules of antidifferentiation:
  • Constant Rule \(:\displaystyle \int kdx=kx+C\)
  • Power Rule:\(\text{where}\,\, n \neq -1: \displaystyle \int X^ndx=\displaystyle \frac{1}{n+1}X^{n+1}+C\))
  • Natural Logarithmic Rule \(:\displaystyle \int \frac{1}{x}dx=lnx+C,x\gt 0\)
  • Exponential Rule(base e) \(: \displaystyle \int e^{ax}dx=\frac{1}{a}e^{ax}+C,\,\, a \neq 0\)
Properties of antidifferentiation
  • A Constant factor can be moved to the front of an indefinite integral\(: \displaystyle \int Cf(x)dx = C \cdot \int f(x)dx\)
  • The antiderivative of a sum or difference is the sum or difference of the antiderivatives\(:\displaystyle \int \displaystyle \left[ f(x) \pm g(x) \right]dx=X^ndx=\displaystyle \int f(x)dx \pm \int g(x)dx\)
